7 Legacy and Continuing Work
8 See Also
9 External Links
Early Life and Background
Datu Muhammad Amin Jammal Khan Lucman was born into two of Mindanao's most distinguished Muslim
families. His maternal lineage traces to the Abbas-Tamano clan, while his paternal heritage comes from the Alonto-
Lucman family—both historically significant in the leadership and governance of Muslim Mindanao. Despite this
noble heritage, Lucman deliberately chose a path grounded in merit rather than privilege, starting his professional
career from the ground level to gain authentic understanding of frontline operations and community realities.
The nickname "Magic" reflects both his initials (MAJK) and his reputation for achieving seemingly impossible
results in challenging environments—from securing telecommunications infrastructure in conflict zones to
pioneering service delivery in areas other providers had written off as too risky or unprofitable.

PAGE 2
Telecommunications Career
Early Years with DITO
Lucman joined DITO Telecommunity Corporation during its early expansion phase and quickly established himself
as a high-impact performer. From the beginning, he was assigned to strategically important but operationally
challenging territories, including Butuan, Bukidnon, Cagayan de Oro, and expansion corridors leading toward
Zamboanga City. These assignments reflected management's confidence in his ability to navigate complex market
dynamics and operational obstacles.
His approach went beyond conventional sales management. In territories where security threats endangered critical
telecommunications infrastructure, Lucman personally engaged in conflict resolution and diplomatic negotiations,
ensuring that network rollout continued despite significant risks. This hands-on leadership style became his
trademark—he didn't manage challenges from an office; he addressed them on the ground, alongside his teams and
the communities they served.
Pioneering Work in Marawi City
One of Lucman's most significant achievements has been his advocacy for and execution of DITO's investment in
Marawi City and surrounding municipalities. Following the devastating 2017 Siege of Marawi,
telecommunications infrastructure in the area was severely damaged, and rebuilding efforts faced numerous
obstacles including security concerns, regulatory complexities, and economic uncertainty.
Lucman championed the business case for serving Marawi, arguing that connectivity was not just commercially
viable but morally imperative for a city rebuilding from catastrophic conflict. Through his efforts, DITO services
became available in parts of Marawi City as well as in nearby municipalities including Marantao and Malabang.
This represented a watershed moment in expanding digital access to historically underserved areas and
demonstrated that commercial objectives and social impact could align.
He also led the telecommunications industry's first-ever motorcade campaign event in Marawi City—an
unprecedented community engagement initiative that strengthened brand presence while respecting local culture
and traditions. No other telecommunications provider in the area had attempted such an innovative approach to
market activation.
Current Role and Responsibilities
As Area Sales Manager, Lucman oversees strategic operations across Lanao del Sur, Lanao del Norte, Misamis
Occidental, and the cities of Dapitan and Dipolog in Zamboanga del Norte. With more than five years of
telecommunications experience, he manages service delivery for DITO's growing subscriber base, which currently
exceeds 17 million nationwide. His territories encompass some of the most geographically challenging and
economically diverse areas in Mindanao, requiring adaptive strategies that balance commercial performance with
social responsibility.
His leadership has consistently delivered strong operational results while maintaining focus on the company's
mission to provide affordable, reliable connectivity to areas traditionally neglected by major telecommunications
providers.

PAGE 3
Public Service and Humanitarian Work
The Siege of Marawi
In 2017, when the Siege of Marawi erupted, Lucman was working as a Project Manager in Quezon City with a
promising corporate trajectory ahead of him. As the crisis unfolded and his hometown descended into chaos, he
made a decision that would define his character: he left his corporate position to return to Marawi and serve on the
frontlines as a rescuer with the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (PDRRMO).
This was not a symbolic gesture or short-term deployment—Lucman immersed himself in the dangerous,
exhausting work of search and rescue operations during one of the Philippines' most intense urban conflicts. He
chose humanity over career advancement, demonstrating extraordinary courage and selfless commitment to his
community at its moment of greatest need. This experience profoundly shaped his understanding of leadership and
reinforced his conviction that positions of authority carry moral obligations that transcend commercial objectives.
Leadership Philosophy
Lucman describes himself as a "hybrid corporate leader"—someone who bridges micro-level operational execution
with macro-level strategic vision. This philosophy stems from his deliberate choice to rise through the ranks from
entry-level positions rather than leveraging his family heritage for accelerated advancement.
He believes that effective leadership requires three foundational elements:
Humility – Leaders must be willing to learn from those they lead and understand operations from the ground up.
Lived Experience – Theoretical knowledge is insufficient; leaders must personally engage with the realities their
teams and communities face.
Strategic Integration – The ability to connect detailed operational knowledge with broader organizational goals
and societal impact.
This approach has allowed him to build credibility with frontline staff, navigate complex stakeholder relationships
in challenging environments, and design strategies grounded in practical realities rather than abstract theory. His
success in high-risk territories stems not from top-down directives but from collaborative problem-solving
informed by deep contextual understanding.
Recognition and Impact
While Lucman has received internal recognition within DITO Telecommunity Corporation for his performance and
leadership, his broader impact extends beyond corporate metrics. He has become a role model for young Filipino
Muslim professionals, demonstrating that success can be achieved through merit, hard work, and authentic
commitment to service rather than reliance on family connections or political patronage.
His work has contributed to measurable improvements in digital inclusion across Mindanao. Thousands of families
in previously unserved or underserved communities now have access to affordable telecommunications services
because of infrastructure investments he championed and executed. In Marawi City specifically, his efforts have
helped restore a sense of normalcy and connection to the outside world for a population still recovering from
traumatic conflict.

PAGE 4
Challenges and Obstacles
Lucman's career has been marked by significant operational challenges:
Security Risks – Operating in areas affected by armed conflict and insurgency required navigating threats to both
personnel and infrastructure.
Regulatory Complexity – Expanding telecommunications services in Mindanao involved managing relationships
with multiple levels of government and diverse stakeholder groups.
Market Skepticism – Convincing corporate leadership to invest in areas perceived as high-risk or low-return
required building compelling business cases backed by ground-level intelligence.
Cultural Navigation – Bridging corporate culture with traditional community structures in Muslim Mindanao
demanded sensitivity, patience, and authentic relationship-building.
Rather than viewing these obstacles as barriers, Lucman approached them as opportunities to demonstrate the
viability of inclusive business models that serve both shareholder and community interests.
Legacy and Continuing Work
Datu Muhammad Amin Jammal Khan "Magic" Lucman represents a new generation of Filipino Muslim leaders—
professionally accomplished, socially conscious, and deeply committed to nation-building through both corporate
excellence and public service. His career trajectory challenges stereotypes about Muslim Mindanao while affirming
the potential for private sector leadership to drive meaningful social impact.
As DITO Telecommunity Corporation continues expanding its network and subscriber base, Lucman remains
focused on ensuring that growth includes rather than bypasses underserved communities. His vision extends
beyond quarterly targets to long-term transformation—using telecommunications infrastructure as a catalyst for
economic opportunity, educational access, and social cohesion in areas still healing from decades of conflict and
neglect.
His story affirms a fundamental truth about leadership: it is not defined by inherited titles or family heritage alone,
but by the willingness to serve, the courage to engage with difficult realities, and the commitment to create lasting
impact where it matters most.

Princess Tarhata Alonto Lucman
Princess Tarhata Alonto-Lucman (June 26, 1926 -- February 26,
2021), widely called Babo a Tatah (Aunt Tarhata) across Lanao,
was a Maranao princess, politician, and peacebuilder who became
the first female governor of Lanao del Sur.
She was born into one of the most prominent political dynasties in
the history of Muslim Mindanao, and she spent nearly a century
using that position to champion governance reform, women's
dignity, and communal peace.
Her life cut a path that very few women of her generation anywhere
in the Philippines could claim: she challenged patriarchal tradition
as a child, broke the gender ceiling of provincial governance as an
adult, stood firm against a dictatorship at great personal cost,
organized resistance from exile, and then came home to negotiate
the release of hostages without firing a single shot.
Both the Senate of the Philippines and the Bangsamoro Parliament
formally honored her memory after her death in 2021.
Contents
1 ROYAL LINEAGE AND FAMILY
2 EARLY LIFE AND EDUCATION
3 POLITICAL CAREER
3.1 Election and Governance Reforms
3.2 Defiance of Martial Law
3.3 Restoration Under the Aquino Administration
4 THE SAUDI ARABIA EXILE
5 THE 1986 MARAWI HOSTAGE CRISIS
6 LEGACY AS PEACEBUILDER
7 CULTURAL SIGNIFICANCE
8 DEATH AND HONORS
9 SEE ALSO
10 REFERENCES
ROYAL LINEAGE AND FAMILY
Tarhata was born on June 26, 1926, in Ramain, Lanao, into the
absolute summit of Maranao royalty.

PAGE 2
Ethnicity
Maranao
Known Titles
"Iron Lady of Lanao"; Babo a Tatah
(Aunt Tarhata)
Notability
Maranao royalty and pioneering
politician from Lanao del Sur; first
female Governor of Lanao del Sur;
peacebuilder and anti-Marcos dissident;
humanitarian in exile; negotiated the
1986 Marawi hostage crisis without
military force
Known For
Breaking gender barriers in Maranao
politics; defying Martial Law;
organizing the Bangsa Moro exile
resistance in Saudi Arabia; personally
negotiating the unconditional release of
kidnapped Carmelite nuns and foreign
missionaries in 1986; refusing her own
government salary and redirecting it to
low-income provincial employees
Her father was Sultan Alauya Alonto of Ramain, a historic
statesman who served as the very first Muslim senator of the
Philippines. Growing up in his household meant that statecraft,
Islamic theology, and the traditional customary law known as adat
were simply part of daily life.
Leadership ran deep through the whole Alonto clan across multiple
generations.
Her brother Senator Domocao Alonto followed their father's path
into Philippine national politics, and he became one of the chief
architects of modern Islamic institutions in the country, helping
establish Mindanao State University and the Philippine Amanah
Bank.
Another brother, Governor Abdulgafor Madki Alonto, served as
Governor of Lanao del Sur from 1959 to 1967 and later represented
the Philippines as a diplomatic ambassador, with his administration
serving as a critical political anchor for the province during a
particularly transitional decade.
The family legacy carried into the next generation as well. Datu
Abul Khayr D. Alonto, the son of Governor Madki Alonto and
Tarhata's nephew, abandoned his law studies at San Beda during the
onset of Martial Law and joined the Moro National Liberation Front
(MNLF) as one of its founding "Top 90" cadres, eventually
becoming its Vice Chairman. He later transitioned into civilian public service as Chairman of the Mindanao
Development Authority (MinDA), a post he held until his passing in 2019.
Tarhata's own marriage brought another layer to this convergence of royal and political power. She chose Sultan
Haroun Rashid Lucman, the Paramount Sultan of Bayang and a prominent congressional representative, as her
husband. Together they became something close to the definitive power couple of Lanao, blending centuries of
royal prestige with the practical authority of modern democratic politics.
This lineage did not merely grant her privilege. It handed her a sense of duty she took seriously for the rest of her
life. Her children carried that tradition forward, including former Lanao del Sur Vice Governor Normalah Alonto
Lucman.
EARLY LIFE AND EDUCATION
Growing up in an era when Maranao customs confined noblewomen firmly to domestic life, Tarhata began defying
expectations almost from the moment she was old enough to remember anything.
When she was five years old, she survived a life-threatening illness after being treated at a Christian-run hospital.
At the time, traditionalists considered this a radical and deeply uncomfortable step, fearing it would open the door
to conversion.
She then defied convention again by pursuing a formal education. She was tutored by American Thomasites,
including an adoptive mentor she called Mrs. Spencer. Tarhata proved to be a child prodigy: when she entered the
public school system, her sharp intellect let her skip several grade levels, landing in Grade 4 at just six years old.

PAGE 3
As a young girl, she traveled frequently to Manila to serve as an English-language translator and aide for her
senator father, absorbing the rhythms of national politics before most children her age had left their hometown.
She dreamed of eventually studying law. But traditional expectations finally caught up with her in Grade 7, when a
dominant maternal uncle decided she had already received more than enough schooling for a woman of her
standing and ordered her to withdraw from formal studies. She obeyed, but she did not stop learning, and she did
not stop pushing.
Years later, she exercised a rare form of personal autonomy for her time and social position by choosing her own
husband, quietly subverting the marital traditions of her era on her own terms.
POLITICAL CAREER
Election and Governance Reforms
In 1971, Tarhata Alonto-Lucman won the election for Governor of Lanao del Sur, shattering what had been an
exclusively male political space.
She did not treat the governorship as ceremonial. Her administration moved quickly to institutionalize
performance-based budgeting across the provincial government, effectively ending the long-entrenched practice
where officials took personal cuts or commissions before public funds ever reached their intended recipients.
She championed regional agricultural modernization under national development programs and launched
aggressive reforestation campaigns to protect the local environment.
She also made a personal decision that became one of the most quietly striking symbols of her tenure: she refused
to keep her official government salary, directing the provincial treasury to distribute her entire paycheck among the
lowest-income employees at the Capitol instead.
Defiance of Martial Law
Her most defining political test arrived in September 1972, when President Ferdinand Marcos Sr. declared Martial
Law across the Philippines.
While many local officials quietly aligned themselves with the Marcos administration out of fear or political
calculation, Governor Alonto-Lucman did not. She openly criticized the dictatorship, provided protection to
dissenters, and quietly backed the growing Moro youth resistance that was fighting for self-determination.
Her defiance infuriated Malacañang Palace. In 1975, the Marcos regime stripped her of her governorship.
Restoration Under the Aquino Administration
Following the 1986 People Power Revolution that ended the Marcos dictatorship, President Corazon Aquino
appointed Tarhata as Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Governor of Lanao del Sur, recognizing her integrity and restoring
her to the helm of her province. She served in that capacity until 1988.

PAGE 4
THE SAUDI ARABIA EXILE
After her removal from office in 1975, Tarhata and her husband Sultan Haroun Rashid Lucman fled to Saudi
Arabia, settling in Riyadh and Jeddah.
For over a decade, their home in exile functioned as far more than a private residence. It became a strategic hub, a
safe house, a diplomatic back-channel, and a welfare center for thousands of Filipinos who had nowhere else to
turn.
Sultan Rashid Lucman organized and chaired the Bangsa Moro Liberation Organization (BMLO) during this
period. Tarhata served as its organizational matriarch, coordinating political networks and smoothing over the
volatile ideological rifts that naturally emerged among exiled Moro leaders, youth activists, and traditional royalty
trying to sustain a resistance movement from thousands of miles away.
The couple used their royal lineage to secure direct access to the Saudi royal family and the Organization of
Islamic Cooperation (OIC), through which they successfully drew international attention to the human rights
situation in Mindanao under Martial Law.
Their home also served as what might best be described as an underground railroad. Thousands of Filipino
Muslims fleeing military violence in Mindanao, along with political dissidents escaping imprisonment in Manila,
arrived in Saudi Arabia with essentially nothing. Tarhata personally managed a vast informal welfare network from
her home, providing food, shelter, documentation assistance, and help finding legitimate employment within the
Kingdom.
The exile years also created an unexpected but historically significant bridge. When mainstream opposition figures
from Manila, including Ninoy Aquino and Jovito Salonga, traveled to the Middle East seeking international support
for the anti-Marcos movement, the Lucman home in Saudi Arabia became the meeting point where the Moro
struggle and the democratic resistance in Manila found common ground.
Sultan Rashid Lucman passed away in Saudi Arabia in 1984 and was buried in the royal burial grounds of the
Kingdom.
Tarhata carried the mantle alone for the final two years of exile, keeping the resistance network operational until
the 1986 EDSA Revolution finally allowed her to bring their work home.
THE 1986 MARAWI HOSTAGE CRISIS
In July 1986, just months after People Power had restored democratic governance, a massive hostage crisis erupted
in Lanao del Sur.
A heavily armed group of rogue rebels, often referred to as a "lost command," kidnapped ten Filipino Carmelite
nuns from their hilltop convent in Marawi City. The kidnappers also seized Fr. Michel de Gigord, a French
Catholic chaplain serving at Mindanao State University, and Brian Lawrence, an American Protestant missionary.
The newly installed Aquino government faced a nightmare calculation: a military rescue operation carried the real
risk of triggering an all-out religious conflict in Mindanao.
Princess Tarhata, recently returned from exile and serving as OIC Governor, stepped directly into the vacuum.
Rather than deploying troops or provincial police, she used what she considered her most effective weapon: the
traditional code of maratabat (royal honor) and her standing as Babo a Tatah.

PAGE 5
She explicitly ordered the Armed Forces of the Philippines to stand down, knowing that a military presence would
only escalate the danger. She then walked directly into the remote rural area where the captors were holding the
hostages, accompanied only by a small, trusted group of clan elders.
Once inside, she confronted the captors directly. Drawing on her authority as a Maranao princess and the daughter
of Sultan Alauya Alonto, she shamed them for violating ancestral Maranao codes of chivalry and Islamic teachings
that strictly forbid the harming of women, travelers, and religious figures.
Her moral authority proved more effective than any armed intervention could have been. She secured the safe,
unconditional release of all ten Carmelite nuns and both foreign missionaries without a single casualty, without a
ransom payment, and without a shot fired.
LEGACY AS PEACEBUILDER
Long after her formal political career ended, Tarhata remained the spiritual and moral center of Lanao.
She earned the title "Iron Lady of Lanao" not just for her record of political courage, but for her persistent and
uncompromising work on peace and communal harmony. In Mindanao, rido (inter-clan feud) is a persistent cycle
where retaliatory violence can stretch across generations. Armed with little more than her royal authority and the
deep personal trust communities placed in her, Babo a Tatah regularly entered active conflict zones to negotiate
peace pacts between warring families.
She supported weapons turn-in initiatives to reduce the circulation of firearms in the province. She frequently
depleted her personal family savings to fund the pilgrimage fares of former rebels traveling to Mecca or Medina as
part of their community rehabilitation.
Her approach to peace was rooted in a holistic sense of social justice. She understood that lasting peace required
more than the silencing of guns; it required people to have reasons to choose peace, and she worked to provide
those reasons.
CULTURAL SIGNIFICANCE
Tarhata Alonto-Lucman served as a living bridge between ancestral Maranao royalty and modern democratic
governance.
She made a deliberate, consistent choice to resist the westernization of public life. At high-profile state dinners,
diplomatic functions, and international events, she wore the traditional Maranao malong, treating it not as a
costume but as a statement about who she was and what she represented.
By occupying the highest echelons of public power in her province while remaining visibly, unapologetically
Maranao, she permanently shifted the socio-cultural landscape of Mindanao.
Her life made a practical argument that conservative families across the region could not easily dismiss: that
educating daughters would strengthen and preserve Maranao society rather than dilute it.
DEATH AND HONORS
Princess Tarhata Alonto-Lucman passed away from a heart attack on February 26, 2021, at the age of 94, at the
Amai Pakpak Medical Center in Marawi City.

PAGE 6
Following her passing, both the Senate of the Philippines and the Bangsamoro Parliament passed official
resolutions honoring her life and legacy, cementing her standing as an enduring icon of peace, good governance,
and Bangsamoro women's leadership.

Oding L. Ma-amor
Vice Chancellor Oding Lacoto Ma-amor, J.D., DPA, is a Filipino
educator, lawyer, and public administrator from Iligan City who
currently serves as Vice Chancellor and Acting Vice President for
Planning and Development of the Mindanao State University (MSU)
System. He also holds the rank of Associate Professor V at the
College of Public Administration, Graduate Studies, on the MSU
Main Campus in Marawi City. Before moving into university
leadership, he spent years in public service as Chief of the
Administration and Finance Division of the Department of Agrarian
Reform (DAR) in Lanao del Sur, where his steady hand behind the
scenes helped shape how the office ran day to day.
Contents
1 Early Life and Education
2 Career
2.1 Department of Agrarian Reform
2.2 Mindanao State University System
2.3 Academic Career
3 Eligibility and Credentials
4 Skills and Interests
5 See Also
6 References
Early Life and Education
Ma-amor built a strong academic foundation across two very
different but complementary fields: law and public administration.
He earned his Juris Doctor (Bachelor of Laws) from the University
of the Visayas in Cebu City in [YEAR], graduating as a Leadership
Awardee. He later pursued his Doctor in Public Administration
(DPA) at Mindanao State University's Main Campus in Marawi City
in [YEAR], where he was recognized once again for leadership, this
time also earning the distinction of College Awardee. That dual
grounding in law and governance would go on to define the shape of
his entire career.

PAGE 2
Drafting the MSU System Strategic Plan
and 10-Point Agenda, and championing
ethics education for future public servants
through his graduate teaching.
Career
Department of Agrarian Reform
Ma-amor's public service roots trace back to his time as Chief of the Administration and Finance Division at the
Department of Agrarian Reform in Lanao del Sur, based in Marawi City, starting in [YEAR]. It was here that he
first showed his knack for building systems from scratch. He developed the office's very first employee manual,
laying out proper business procedures and office guidelines where none had existed before. He also led the launch
of "DARAYO," the Provincial Office's first ever quarterly newsletter, giving the office a consistent voice for
sharing updates internally and with the public. On top of these, he spearheaded major office improvements as
division chief, work that reflected his broader instinct for organizing people and processes toward clearer, more
efficient outcomes. His reliability on the job was such that he was frequently tapped as Officer-in-Charge whenever
the head of the Provincial Agrarian Reform Office II stepped out on official business, a role that speaks to the trust
placed in him by his superiors.
Mindanao State University System
Ma-amor now holds one of the more demanding posts in Philippine higher education administration as Vice
Chancellor and Acting Vice President for Planning and Development of the MSU System. In this capacity, he
spearheaded the formulation of the MSU System Strategic Plan, led the drafting of the MSU System 10-Point
Agenda, and finalized the MSU Land Use Development and Infrastructure Program (LUDIP), three major
undertakings that continue to guide the university's direction going forward.
He also chaired the institutionalization of PRIME-HRM (Program to Institutionalize Meritocracy and Excellence in
Human Resource Management) within the university system. His committee work runs deep: he served as Overall
Chairperson of the Planning and Development Committee, Chairperson of the Organizational Structure and
Staffing Pattern Committee, and Chairperson of the Income-Generating Projects Committee. He additionally took
on the role of Vice-Chairperson for the Infrastructure Design, OSR Green, Smart, and Resilient Committee, the
Policy on Governance Committee, and the Comprehensive Anti-Smoking and Tobacco Control Policy and
Guidelines Committee, a wide-ranging portfolio that touches nearly every corner of university governance.
Academic Career
Alongside his administrative duties, Ma-amor continues to teach as Associate Professor V at the College of Public
Administration, Graduate Studies, MSU Main Campus. He handles graduate-level instruction in Public Ethics and
Accountability, where he pushes students to think critically about ethical governance and the responsibilities that
come with public office. He also teaches Introduction to Planning and Local Government, walking students
through the foundational concepts of governance, public administration, and local development. Beyond his home
campus, he has served as a lecturer for numerous local and international trainings and seminars, extending his
influence well past MSU's classrooms.
Eligibility and Credentials
Ma-amor holds several professional eligibilities recognized under Philippine civil service standards, including the
CSC Police Officer Eligibility, the Career Service Professional Eligibility, and the PD 907 Honor Graduate
Eligibility.

PAGE 3
Skills and Interests
Colleagues and students alike describe Ma-amor as organized, resourceful, analytical, collaborative, and results-
oriented, traits that show clearly in the range of committees and projects he has led. He is proficient in the
Microsoft Office suite (Excel, Word, and PowerPoint), tools he relies on heavily in both his administrative and
teaching work. His professional interests center on strategic planning, local governance, academic and policy
research, and educational leadership, threads that run consistently through both halves of his career.

title: Mabaning, Ainul Yaqiin M.
text:
PAGE 1
Ainul Yaqiin M. Mabaning
Ainul Yaqiin M. Mabaning is a Maranao human resources executive, strategic communications specialist, and
business leader known for building organizational excellence across corporate, non-profit, and entrepreneurial
sectors. Currently serving as Chief Executive Officer of Batal Human Resource Services since October 2024, she
brings more than two decades of integrated HR, leadership development, and communications expertise to her
roles. Her career trajectory reflects a distinctive commitment to strategic vision, integrity, and professional
excellence grounded in her Maranao cultural identity. Mabaning is perhaps best recognized for her award-winning
contributions to professional communications and leadership, earning international recognition through
Toastmasters International achievements while building substantive impact in organizational transformation and
talent development.
Contents
1 Early Life and Background
2 Education
3 Career
3.1 Early Teaching and International Experience
3.2 HR and Communications Leadership at Schedio Consulting

7 Personal Values and Interests
8 See Also
9 Further Reading
Early Life and Background
Ainul Yaqiin M. Mabaning was born and raised in Iligan City, a major industrial and commercial hub on the island
of Mindanao. As a native Maranao speaker fluent in professional English, conversational Bisaya, and
conversational Arabic, she grew up navigating multiple cultural and linguistic contexts that would later define her
approach to organizational leadership and cross-cultural communication. Her upbringing in Iligan exposed her to
the entrepreneurial spirit of the region and the professional culture of its business community. Her native fluency in
Maranao reflects deep roots in the broader Bangsamoro cultural heritage, while her multilingual competence and
international exposure shaped her perspective on leadership as a bridge between local identity and global
professional standards.

PAGE 2

The formative experiences of her childhood in Iligan would
resurface later in her entrepreneurial ventures, including her
ownership and management of Big Poppa's Diner, which she
established in 2020 and operated successfully while maintaining
her executive roles. This balance between professional
management and community-rooted enterprise reflects a
characteristic philosophy: that organizational excellence need not
be disconnected from cultural grounding or local roots.
Education
Mabaning completed her undergraduate education at Columbus
University in Mississippi, United States, where she earned a
Bachelor of Science in Business Administration with a major in
Marketing in 2006. Her undergraduate focus on marketing
provided foundational knowledge in consumer behavior, brand
strategy, and organizational communications that would inform
her later work in HR consulting and leadership development.
She advanced her education through the prestigious Asian Institute
of Management (AIM), where she earned her Master of Business
Administration degree between 2010 and 2011. The AIM program
is recognized as one of Asia's leading business schools and
emphasizes strategic leadership, organizational behavior, and
integrated business management. Her MBA equipped her with
advanced frameworks for strategic planning, organizational
transformation, and executive leadership that proved instrumental
in her subsequent career progression.
Career
Early Teaching and International Experience
Mabaning began her professional career in education, serving as a
College Instructor and Administrative Coordinator at the
International Philippine School in Riyadh, Kingdom of Saudi
Arabia, from 2007 to 2012. She taught Marketing, Business Law,
Economics, and Financial Management while managing HR-
related functions including timekeeping, recruitment, onboarding,
and employee experience initiatives. This role marked her entry
into the integrated practice of HR and organizational development,
setting a pattern she would expand throughout her career:
combining institutional knowledge with hands-on people
management.
Her time in Riyadh expanded her cultural competency and
international professional networks, exposing her to the diverse
challenges of managing multinational education organizations and

PAGE 3
preparing her for later roles in international consulting and cross-cultural communications.
HR and Communications Leadership at Schedio Consulting
From 2012 to 2018, Mabaning served as Senior Manager of HR, Administration, and Communications at Schedio
Consulting Inc. in Makati City. This role consolidated her expertise across three integrated domains. In the HR
function, she managed end-to-end staffing from recruiting through onboarding, designed compensation strategies
based on market research, developed performance management frameworks, and conducted strategic HR planning
with emphasis on retention. Her administrative responsibilities included operational improvements and financial
reporting. On the communications side, she led development of the company's Communications Plan and created
strategies supporting organizational goals and brand reach.
This position reflected her growing sophistication in organizational design and her ability to manage competing
priorities across domains typically siloed in other organizations. Her approach integrated HR strategy with internal
and external communications, recognizing that talent management and organizational messaging operate as
interconnected systems.
Red Cross and Development Work
Between 2018 and 2019, Mabaning served as Communications Officer for the International Committee of the Red
Cross (ICRC) in Iligan City. The role built on her communications expertise while introducing her to the non-profit
humanitarian sector. She developed and executed communication strategies for organizational programs and
beneficiaries, handled external relations, created content, and coordinated community engagement initiatives. This
experience deepened her understanding of communications as a tool for social impact and organizational
accountability.
In 2018, she earned recognition as Chief Training Expert in Communications During Crisis through the ICRC, a
credential that speaks to her depth in managing organizational messaging under challenging circumstances.
Senior Delivery Management at the Asian Development Bank
From 2021 to 2023, Mabaning served as Senior Delivery Manager at Talentium Inc., managing the Asian
Development Bank (ADB) Special IT Team responsible for eLearning and video output production. She managed
HR functions including onboarding, payroll, timesheet management, benefits, and employee relations while
leading AGILE project management and ensuring timely delivery of major outputs. This role required her to blend
technical project management with personnel management, coordinating stakeholder communications across
development finance institutions and technology teams.
During this period, she was appointed as Project Management Resource Speaker for the ADB and Talentium,
delivering expertise in organizational project delivery across the Asia-Pacific region.
Human Resources Director at Arlene de Castro Law Firm
From November 2023 to February 2024, Mabaning served as Human Resources Director at Arlene de Castro Law
Firm in Bonifacio Global City, Taguig. In this brief but intensive role, she collaborated with the Managing Partner
and Core Group on HR goals, staffing strategies, and workforce planning. She planned and implemented HR
policies, processes, training, and organizational development initiatives. Internally, she administered
comprehensive HR programs including compensation, benefits, leave management, disciplinary matters, and

PAGE 4
performance management. Externally, she designed and implemented HR consulting products, supervised external
projects, and attended exploratory sessions with prospective clients. She also served as Webinar Resource Speaker
for the firm's HR-focused programs during this period.
Chief Executive Officer of Batal Human Resource Services
In October 2024, Mabaning assumed the position of Chief Executive Officer of Batal Human Resource Services,
her current role. As CEO, she provides overall strategic leadership and direction across all service lines, including
HR Consulting, Talent Solutions, Leadership Development Programs, and Client Advisory Services. She leads
business development initiatives, client acquisition, and partnership expansion while directing the creation and
refinement of HR frameworks, training modules, and leadership methodologies. She supervises operations, finance,
HR, marketing, and service delivery teams, represents the company in speaking engagements and corporate
training events, and maintains direct oversight of key client accounts and large-scale HR projects. This role
represents the culmination of her career trajectory: from integrated functional expertise to executive strategic
leadership.
Entrepreneurship: Big Poppa's Diner
Since 2020, Mabaning has served as Owner and General Manager of Big Poppa's Diner in Iligan City, managing
full operational aspects including HR, finance, administration, and marketing. She oversees staffing, vendor
relations, quality control, and customer experience while building the restaurant's brand and market position. In
2022, the diner earned recognition as 1st Runner Up in the Best Halal Restaurant Category at the Iligan Business
Awards, a testament to her ability to integrate professional hospitality management with culturally grounded
product and service excellence.
Professional Recognition and Speaking Engagements
Mabaning's professional achievements extend significantly into communications and public leadership through her
work with Toastmasters International, where she achieved multiple championships and leadership roles. These
recognitions underscore her expertise in persuasive communication, organizational speaking, and leadership
presence.
Between 1998 and 2001, she earned four major international titles: Table Topics City Champion with Riyadh
Toastmasters (1998), Centennial Best Debate Speaker of the Philippines awarded by the Philippine Embassy
(1998), International Speech Contest Champion for the Middle East region (2000), and International Evaluation
Master Champion for the Middle East region (2001). In 2001, she served as Chief Judge for the International
Conference of Toastmasters in Bahrain, reflecting her standing within the organization.
Beyond Toastmasters, she has been engaged as Chief Trainer for Islamic Banking Opportunities for SMEs through
Amanah Bank (2017), Chief Training Expert for Communications During Crisis through the International
Committee of the Red Cross (2018), and as Webinar Resource Speaker and Session Chair for the South East Asian
Symposium and Expo in Quezon City (2025). These appointments reflect her recognition as a subject matter expert
in organizational communications, HR strategy, and professional development.
Contributions to Organizational Excellence
Mabaning's career reflects a consistent commitment to building systems of organizational excellence across diverse
sectors. Her contributions span several domains:

PAGE 5
HR Strategy and Talent Development. She has designed comprehensive HR frameworks, compensation
structures, and performance management systems for organizations ranging from law firms to multinational
education providers to development finance institutions. Her work emphasizes the integration of market-based
compensation strategy with talent retention and organizational culture.
Communications and Organizational Messaging. She has led the development of organizational
communications plans, content strategies, and external messaging for enterprises and non-profits. Her approach
treats communications as integral to organizational strategy rather than peripheral to it, linking internal alignment
with external brand positioning.
Leadership Development and Professional Communications. Her Toastmasters achievements and subsequent
training roles demonstrate deep expertise in developing leaders' communication capabilities, persuasive speaking,
and presence. Her training in communications during crisis situations reflects her ability to support organizations
through high-stakes messaging scenarios.
Organizational Transformation. Across multiple roles, she has managed the change management, staffing, and
operational dimensions of organizational transitions, from establishing new service lines to expanding market
reach.
Legacy and Cultural Significance
Mabaning's career arc embodies a distinctive bridge between international professional excellence and Maranao
cultural identity. As a native Maranao speaker who earned Toastmasters championships, pursued an MBA from
Asia's leading business schools, and built executive leadership across the region, she represents the expanding
presence of Maranao women in strategic organizational roles and professional leadership. Her fluency in Maranao,
alongside professional English and conversational Arabic, reflects a multilingual competence often
underrepresented in executive ranks.
Her success as an entrepreneur through Big Poppa's Diner, achieving recognition in the Iligan Business Awards
while maintaining her executive roles, demonstrates her capacity to build culturally rooted enterprises alongside
institutional leadership. This integration of professional excellence with cultural grounding offers a model distinct
from narratives that treat cultural identity and corporate advancement as competing rather than complementary
dimensions of leadership.
Her legacy centers on strategic organizational building grounded in integrity and dedicated to developing others.
Throughout her career, she has invested in talent development, organizational systems, and leadership
communications as mechanisms for sustainable enterprise. Her current role as CEO of Batal HR Services positions
her to scale these contributions across the Philippine business landscape.
Personal Values and Interests
Mabaning's professional philosophy, as articulated in her professional summary, emphasizes dedication, strategic
vision, and strong integrity. In her personal life, she maintains active interests in volleyball, badminton, music, and
oration. Her advanced standing as a Toastmaster Silver and her recognition as a Communications Expert reflect
sustained commitment to the discipline of public speaking and leadership communication. Her coaching and
mentoring skills, documented across multiple roles, indicate a personal investment in developing others.

PAGE 6

Nawawi Malaco Mabaning
Datu Nawawi "Wawi" Malaco Mabaning (died 2024) was a
distinguished Maranao professional, banking executive, and
community leader whose career spanned excellence in athletics,
finance, and organizational leadership across three decades in the
Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
Born in Marinaut as the only son of Datu a Masla Ramain
Abdulazis Mabaning and Bae Pocandang Malaco, he carried
forward a proud Maranao lineage rooted in honor and
responsibility.
His most enduring legacy lies not only in his corporate
achievements but in his unwavering commitment to uplifting
Overseas Filipino Workers and developing leaders through
communication and personal excellence.
Contents
1 Early Life and Athletic Achievement
2 Professional Career in Saudi Arabia
3 Service to Overseas Filipino Workers
4 Leadership in Toastmasters International
5 Legacy and Character
6 Further Reading
7 See Also
Early Life and Athletic Achievement
In his formative years, Datu Nawawi demonstrated exceptional
focus and discipline that would define his entire career.
He earned the distinction of becoming a Philippine National Gold Medalist in Archery during the 1970s, a feat that
reflected precision, patience, and an unyielding commitment to mastery.
This early accomplishment in sport revealed the character he would later bring to his professional endeavors: the
willingness to excel through dedication and the pursuit of excellence in all endeavors.
Professional Career in Saudi Arabia
Datu Nawawi embarked on a remarkable professional journey spanning more than three decades in the banking
sector of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
He rose through the ranks to assume the position of Senior Executive Manager for Credit Risk at Banque Saudi
Fransi, Head Office in Riyadh, a major Saudi financial institution.

PAGE 2
Over the course of 34 years of dedicated service, he became known throughout the banking community for his
analytical excellence, integrity, and steady leadership in managing complex financial responsibilities.
He retired in 2015 after earning the respect and admiration of colleagues and industry leaders alike.
His career demonstrated that excellence transcends geographic boundaries, and that a Filipino professional could
command respect and achieve advancement in one of the world's most rigorous financial sectors.
Service to Overseas Filipino Workers
Beyond his corporate achievements, Datu Nawawi remained profoundly committed to the welfare and
representation of Overseas Filipino Workers in the Middle East.
In 1998, he made history by becoming the only Maranao elected to represent Filipino workers in the newly formed
OFW Congress of Saudi Arabia.
His election through a democratic process reflected the confidence and esteem in which he was held by the broader
Filipino community in the Kingdom.
His representation was marked by genuine advocacy for worker rights, inclusivity across all ethnic groups, and a
sincere dedication to improving the lives and working conditions of his fellow Filipinos abroad.
This role placed him at the forefront of efforts to organize and give voice to some of the most vulnerable segments
of the migrant workforce.
Leadership in Toastmasters International
Recognizing the power of effective communication as a tool for personal and professional development, Datu
Nawawi became an active member of Toastmasters International in the Gulf region.
He achieved the prestigious rank of Distinguished Toastmaster (DTM), one of the highest honors within the
organization, reflecting mastery in public speaking, leadership, and mentorship.
More significantly, he became the first Maranao Overseas Filipino Worker in the Middle East to earn this
distinction and to serve as an Area Governor in Gulf Toastmasters.
In these roles, he helped shape future leaders, fostering a culture of excellence in communication, personal
development, and ethical leadership among Filipinos working in the Gulf.
His contributions to Toastmasters demonstrated his belief that empowerment through education and skill
development was as vital as material assistance.
Legacy and Character
Datu Nawawi's life was a testament to what can be achieved through discipline, humility, and a profound sense of
purpose.
He exemplified the values of a leader who excelled in his professional field while simultaneously lifting others
along his journey.

PAGE 3
His career bridged multiple worlds: the demanding corporate environment of international banking, the informal
networks of migrant worker communities, and the structured leadership development of Toastmasters.
In each arena, he brought the same commitment to integrity, excellence, and service that defined his character.
His passing in 2024 marked the end of an era for those who knew him, yet his influence continues through those he
mentored, those whose lives he improved, and the example he set of what a Filipino professional could achieve
abroad.

Saga D. Mabaning
Atty. Saga D. Mabaning is a distinguished Maranao legal professional, public servant, and youth advocate whose
career has centered on electoral integrity, Bangsamoro regional governance, and the empowerment of Muslim
youth through values-based leadership and interfaith dialogue. His work bridges high-level legal policy with
grassroots youth mentorship, reflecting a lifetime commitment to integrating Islamic principles with modern
democratic governance in the emerging Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).
Contents
1 Early Life and Cultural Foundation
2 Education and Legal Formation
3 Professional Career
3.1 Role at the Commission on Elections
3.2 Legal Contributions to the Bangsamoro Electoral Code
3.3 World Assembly of Muslim Youth (WAMY) Philippines
4 Contributions to Interfaith Harmony
5 Recognition of Bangsamoro Qur'anic Excellence
6 Personal Philosophy and Values
7 Recognition and Representation
8 Legacy and Ongoing Work
9 Further Reading
10 See Also
Early Life and Cultural Foundation
Atty. Mabaning belongs to the Maranao ethnic group, the "People of
the Lake," whose heartland centers on Lanao del Sur in the
Bangsamoro region. Growing up immersed in a culture deeply rooted
in Islamic tradition and Maranao custom, his upbringing emphasized
the values of Maratabat (dignity and honor), community
responsibility, and education as a pathway to service. The Maranao
worldview, shaped by both pre-Islamic and Islamic heritage, taught
him early that education and integrity were not personal
achievements but duties owed to family, community, and faith.
His formative years in Lanao del Sur connected him to the region's
rich intellectual and spiritual traditions. The province has long
produced scholars, leaders, and advocates who navigate the complex
terrain of faith, governance, and cultural preservation. Mabaning's own journey followed this pattern, blending
secular legal training with a lifelong engagement with Islamic jurisprudence and Bangsamoro political
development.

PAGE 2
Education and Legal Formation
Mabaning earned his Juris Doctor (JD) degree through rigorous academic study in the Philippines, building the
legal foundation that would enable him to practice before the Philippine Bar and work at the intersection of law and
public administration. His legal education was not merely secular. Throughout his studies and practice, he remained
committed to understanding how Islamic jurisprudence (Fiqh) and modern constitutional law could coexist and
strengthen democratic governance in the BARMM.
His formation as a lawyer occurred during a transformative period in Philippine legal history. The move toward
Muslim autonomy and later the passage of the Bangsamoro Organic Law created urgent need for legal experts who
understood both national constitutional frameworks and the aspirations of Bangsamoro peoples for self-
governance. Mabaning positioned himself to answer that need.
Professional Career
Role at the Commission on Elections
Atty. Mabaning served as a Director at the Commission on Elections (COMELEC), one of the Philippines' three
constitutional commissions. In this capacity, he played a vital role in managing electoral processes and addressing
critical issues such as the relationship between technology and democratic integrity in the Philippines' voting
systems.
His work at COMELEC coincided with a pivotal moment in Philippine electoral history. The move toward
BARMM's first parliamentary elections required new legal frameworks and careful coordination between national
electoral bodies and regional governance structures. As a COMELEC Director, Mabaning contributed to
discussions about how the national electoral body could support the BARMM's unique parliamentary system while
maintaining the standards expected of Philippine elections.
Legal Contributions to the Bangsamoro Electoral Code
Mabaning's most significant legal contribution has been his instrumental role in shaping and advising on the
Bangsamoro Electoral Code, formally enacted as Bangsamoro Autonomy Act (BAA) No. 35 in March 2023. This
landmark legislation established the legal framework for electoral governance in the BARMM and reflects careful
negotiation between regional autonomy and national constitutional requirements.<ref>Bangsamoro Electoral Code
of 2023, Articles I-VI, Bangsamoro Gazette. 2023.</ref>
His specific contributions to the Electoral Code centered on several critical areas:
Structural Alignment: He was a key voice in ensuring that the Electoral Code remained consistent with
national election laws while accommodating the BARMM's innovative parliamentary form of government.
This required translating the Bangsamoro Organic Law's framework into practical electoral procedures.
Party System Architecture: Mabaning provided legal guidance during the transition from traditional
localized elective structures to the party-centered model that defines the BARMM Parliament. This shift
represents a fundamental change in how Bangsamoro governance operates, moving from individual-based
contests to party-based representation with proportional allocation.
Electoral Integrity and Moral Governance: He has been a vocal advocate for the Electoral Code's "moral
governance" provisions, which aim to foster genuinely principled political parties and reduce the influence of

PAGE 3
political dynasties in the region. His position reflects a belief that electoral codes do more than manage
voting logistics. They shape the character of political life.
Addressing Constitutional Complexities: Mabaning has engaged with the legal challenges surrounding
redistricting laws and the multiple postponements of BARMM elections. The exclusion of Sulu from the
BARMM by Supreme Court order created unprecedented legal and constitutional questions about how to
allocate parliamentary seats fairly. His work has focused on ensuring that the legal roadmap for elections
remains constitutionally sound despite these challenges.
World Assembly of Muslim Youth (WAMY) Philippines
Beyond his government roles, Atty. Mabaning has emerged as a prominent figure within the World Assembly of
Muslim Youth (WAMY) Philippines, an international Islamic educational organization committed to youth
leadership development and interfaith understanding. WAMY operates in 56 countries and is recognized by the
United Nations as a humanitarian and relief-works organization.<ref>World Assembly of Muslim Youth. "About
WAMY." UN Yearbook Profile. Retrieved 2024.</ref>
Within WAMY Philippines, Mabaning has served as both mentor and director, focusing on values-based leadership
for young Muslims navigating multicultural societies. His philosophy, often encapsulated in the phrase "You Are
the Leader," challenges youth to take initiative regardless of their current status or position. This teaching reflects
both Islamic concepts of responsibility (Amanah) and the Maranao tradition of community leadership.
He has represented the Philippines at international youth forums, including the Australia-Southeast Asia Muslim
Youth Summit, where he has spoken on the role of young Muslims in multicultural democracies and the integration
of traditional values with global standards. His mentorship emphasizes that leadership is a trust placed by the
community and that Muslims in the 21st century must engage in both spiritual formation and practical skill
development.
Contributions to Interfaith Harmony
A defining thread in Mabaning's public work has been his advocacy for interfaith dialogue and mutual
understanding between Muslims and Christians in Mindanao. He has been a vocal proponent of highlighting
theological similarities between Islam and Christianity, particularly in their shared emphasis on justice, mercy, and
human dignity. This work carries significant weight in Mindanao's context, where decades of conflict have left
deep communal wounds.
His interfaith initiatives seek to move beyond symbolic gestures toward substantive engagement. By bringing
together Muslim and Christian leaders to discuss shared values and common concerns, he has worked to
demonstrate that religious difference need not produce enmity and that shared governance frameworks can respect
faith commitments on all sides.
Recognition of Bangsamoro Qur'anic Excellence
Mabaning has been instrumental in promoting government recognition of Bangsamoro Qur'an reciters and scholars,
elevating the status of Islamic spiritual education within the region's official identity. The BARMM has
increasingly recognized that preserving Bangsamoro culture includes honoring the region's tradition of Qur'anic
scholarship and recitation.

PAGE 4
His advocacy in this area reflects a conviction that regional identity encompasses spiritual heritage. For Muslim
Filipinos, and particularly for Maranaos, the Qur'an represents not merely a religious text but a foundation of
civilization, culture, and learning. By promoting the recognition of accomplished reciters and scholars, Mabaning
has helped embed Islamic intellectual tradition within the BARMM's official identity and institutional structures.
Personal Philosophy and Values
Mabaning's life and work are guided by three foundational principles: integrity, service, and faith. These are not
abstract ideals but lived commitments evident in how he approaches professional challenges and mentors young
people.
His philosophy bridges the traditional Maranao value of Maratabat (dignity, honor, and proper conduct) with the
Islamic concept of Ihsan (excellence in service and worship). In his teaching and advocacy, he suggests that leaders
must pursue Ihsan in every action, striving not merely to meet minimum legal or professional standards but to
exemplify excellence in thought, speech, and deed. This fusion of cultural and religious values gives his work a
distinctive character.
The concept of Amanah (trust, responsibility) is central to his mentorship philosophy. Leaders, in his view, do not
hold power for personal advancement. They hold a trust on behalf of their community. This understanding shapes
how he approaches both legal work in government and mentorship in youth organizations.
Recognition and Representation
Mabaning has represented the Philippines and the Bangsamoro at multiple international forums, including Global
Youth Summit initiatives focused on sustainable development and community resilience. These platforms have
allowed him to articulate Bangsamoro perspectives on youth leadership, Islamic governance, and peacebuilding to
global audiences.
His participation in regional dialogues on peace and development reflects the BARMM's positioning within
broader Indo-Pacific conversations about governance innovation and religious plurality. By bringing Bangsamoro
voices to these forums, he has helped ensure that the region's unique experiences and insights contribute to global
thinking about democracy, faith, and social development.
Legacy and Ongoing Work
Atty. Saga D. Mabaning's career exemplifies the generation of Bangsamoro leaders who have embraced the task of
building democratic institutions grounded in both constitutional principles and Islamic values. His contributions to
the Bangsamoro Electoral Code have created a legal foundation for parliamentary democracy in the BARMM. His
mentorship through WAMY has shaped young Muslim leaders who will navigate the 21st century. His advocacy
for interfaith understanding has built bridges in a region learning to move beyond conflict.
His work remains ongoing. The first regular Bangsamoro Parliament election, now scheduled for September 14,
2026, will test the electoral framework to which Mabaning contributed significantly. The youth he has mentored
will carry his teachings about integrity, service, and excellence into their own leadership roles. The interfaith
dialogues he has initiated will continue to bear fruit in communities where Muslims and Christians work together
for common development.

PAGE 5
The signature of Mabaning's legacy is this: he has insisted that law and governance are not merely technical
matters. They are expressions of community values and reflections of fundamental commitments to justice, dignity,
and the common good. In bridging legal expertise with spiritual principle, in connecting youth empowerment with
electoral integrity, he has modeled what it means to serve the Bangsamoro not as an administrator but as a steward
of its future.
Further Reading

text:

Habib Watamama Macaayong
Habib Watamama Macaayong (also written as Habib W.
Macaayong) is a distinguished Meranaw academician,
administrator, and peace advocate from Bacolod-Kalawi, Lanao
del Sur.
He served as the 7th Regular President (10th overall) of the
Mindanao State University (MSU) System from 2016 to 2022,
leading the country's most prominent Muslim-majority university
through some of its most defining and difficult chapters.<ref
name="pia2021">Philippine Information Agency. (2021, October
28). Macaayong underscores MSU System's administrative
reforms. https://mirror.pia.gov.ph/news/2021/10/28/macaayong-
underscores-msu-systems-administrative-reforms</ref>
In the Bangsamoro world, Dr. Macaayong is remembered as a
president who showed up when it mattered most. He stayed on
campus during the five-month Marawi Siege of 2017, rallied the
community with the "Balik MSU" campaign, and made MSU-
Marawi the first city institution to reopen its gates after the battle,
turning rubble into resolve.
Beyond crisis leadership, he spent decades shaping policy at the
national level, having chaired the technical working group on
power sharing during the historic Government-MILF peace
negotiations from 2004 to 2013.
His peers and the communities he served have called him the
"Peace President" of Mindanao State University, a title that
speaks to both his role in formal negotiations and his quiet,
persistent work of keeping a university together across lines of
faith, politics, and conflict.
Contents
1 Background
2 Education
3 Early Career at SPDA (1975–1981)
4 Academic Career
5 Presidency of the MSU System (2016 to 2022)
5.1 Leadership During the 2017 Marawi Siege
5.2 COVID-19 Response
5.3 Infrastructure and Campus Modernization
5.4 Personnel Reform and Faculty Promotion
5.5 Academic Accreditation and Quality Assurance
6 Values and Leadership Philosophy

PAGE 2
7 Legacy
8 Recognition
9 Challenges
10 See Also
11 External Links
Background
Dr. Macaayong's roots run deep in the Lanao region.
A proud son of Bacolod-Kalawi in Lanao del Sur, he belongs to the Meranaw ethnic group, one of the thirteen
recognized Bangsamoro peoples and the primary inhabitants of the Lake Lanao basin.
His upbringing in this culturally rich and politically complex region shaped his worldview early on, giving him a
direct, lived understanding of what it means to navigate identity, faith, and governance in Muslim Mindanao.
Those roots never left him, even as his career took him to national policy rooms and international dialogue tables.
They kept him grounded in the realities of the community that MSU was always meant to serve.<ref name="fb-
kimalo">Abdullah, K. M. (n.d.). Post about Habib W. Macaayong. Facebook.
https://www.facebook.com/KimalodenMayonAbdullah/posts/122171562620893556/</ref>
Education
Dr. Macaayong built his academic foundation in governance and public administration, disciplines that prepared
him equally for the classroom, the negotiating table, and the president's office.
The specific institutions and degrees earned are consistent with the profile of a career academic who rose through
the ranks of the MSU system over more than three decades of teaching and research.
Early Career at SPDA (1975–1981)
Immediately following his graduation from Mindanao State University (MSU) in 1975, Dr. Habib Watamama
Macaayong began his professional career with the Southern Philippines Development Administration (now
Authority or SPDA). His employment at SPDA is historically significant as the agency was established that same
year—on April 22, 1975, via Presidential Decree No. 690—to address the economic and social development of
Mindanao, Sulu, and Tawi-Tawi.
As a young graduate in Public Administration, Macaayong joined SPDA during its foundational years. His role was
aligned with the agency's primary mandate to foster balanced growth and national integration in the region.
• Project Involvement: During his tenure, he was involved in the early implementation of corporate and social
projects, ranging from agro-industrial ventures to peace and development initiatives. • Transition to Academe: His
practical experience in regional development at SPDA served as a bridge to his academic career; he transitioned
from government administration to the Mindanao State University as a professor in 1981.

PAGE 3
Academic Career
Before taking on the presidency, Dr. Macaayong had already given more than thirty years of his professional life to
Mindanao State University.
He joined the MSU College of Public Affairs as a faculty member in 1981 and rose to the rank of Professor VI, the
highest rank in the Philippine professorial system, teaching governance, public administration, and policy for over
35 years.<ref name="msuiit-news">MSU-IIT Information Office. (n.d.). News detail.
https://www.msuiit.edu.ph/news/news-detail.php?id=771</ref>
That kind of tenure, three and a half decades in the same institution, isn't just longevity. It's a record of trust, a sign
that he kept growing and that his students and colleagues kept coming back.
His classroom work was paired with serious national engagement. From 2004 to 2013, Dr. Macaayong served as
chairman of the technical working group on power sharing during the GPH-MILF peace negotiations,
contributing directly to the policy architecture that would eventually shape the Bangsamoro peace process.
It was rare, and significant, for an academic to hold that kind of role in formal negotiations, and it reflected the
depth of his expertise in governance and his standing in both Muslim and national circles.
Presidency of the MSU System (2016 to 2022)
Dr. Macaayong was appointed as the 7th Regular President (10th overall) of the Mindanao State University
System in 2016, a position he held until 2022.<ref name="inquirer-naming">Inquirer News. (n.d.). Naming of new
MSU president draws fire. https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/780806/naming-of-new-msu-president-draws-fire</ref>
His six-year tenure was one of the most eventful in the university's history, bracketed on one side by a major armed
conflict and on the other by a global pandemic.
Leadership During the 2017 Marawi Siege
When the Marawi Siege broke out in May 2017, most people were trying to leave the city. Dr. Macaayong stayed.
He remained on campus throughout the five-month conflict, overseeing security operations and working to protect
what he could of the university's people, assets, and continuity.
When the dust settled, he launched the "Balik MSU" campaign, a community-driven initiative to bring students,
faculty, and staff back to campus.
The result was historic: MSU-Marawi became the first institution in Marawi City to reopen after the siege, a
powerful symbol of institutional resilience and Meranaw determination in the face of extremism.
In a city where entire neighborhoods had been reduced to rubble, the reopening of MSU was more than a logistical
achievement. It was a statement that the community would not be defined by the siege.
COVID-19 Response
When the COVID-19 pandemic struck in 2020 and disrupted academic life across the country, Dr. Macaayong's
administration responded with a policy that prioritized students over bureaucratic convention.

PAGE 4
The Mass Promotion policy of 2020 allowed students to move forward in their academic journey despite the
disruptions of the pandemic, acknowledging both the academic and financial hardships that families across the
MSU system were facing.
It was a pragmatic, compassionate call, and it reflected a consistent thread in his leadership: when rules and
realities collide, he leaned toward the people.
Infrastructure and Campus Modernization
One of the most visible legacies of his presidency is the physical transformation of the MSU system's campuses.
Under Dr. Macaayong's watch, the university completed major construction and modernization projects, including
the Science and Technology Building, the College of Social Sciences and Humanities Building, and the
installation of a campus-wide fiber optic network.
These weren't cosmetic upgrades. They were investments in the university's capacity to teach, research, and
compete, laying the groundwork for academic programs to qualify for higher accreditation levels in the years that
followed.
Personnel Reform and Faculty Promotion
One of the quieter but deeply consequential reforms of his administration was the revival of the university's Merit
Selection Board.
By reactivating the board and instituting a transparent promotion process, Dr. Macaayong's administration was able
to push through the massive promotion of over 900 faculty members, some of whom had been stuck in the same
rank for decades.<ref name="pia2021"/><ref name="fb-ateshy">Facebook Post. (n.d.). Former MSU President
Habib W. Macaayong: a transformative leader. https://www.facebook.com/ateshy143/posts/former-msu-president-
habib-w-macaayong-a-transformative-leader-who-built-a-lasti/1547883490318048/</ref>
For those faculty members and their families, it was a life-changing development. For the university, it was a reset:
a recommitment to merit as the basis of advancement, not politics or seniority alone.
Academic Accreditation and Quality Assurance
Under Dr. Macaayong, the MSU System made aggressive strides in program accreditation and compliance.
By the end of his term in 2021, MSU-Marawi was recognized by the Accrediting Agency of Chartered Colleges
and Universities in the Philippines (AACCUP) as the Top 1 Performing State University and College (SUC)
in the country, based on the highest number of Level I accredited programs, reaching a milestone of 40 Level I
programs.<ref name="fb-msumain">Mindanao State University Main Campus. (n.d.). MSU-Marawi cited as Top
1 Performing SUC. Facebook. https://www.facebook.com/msumain.edu.ph/posts/the-mindanao-state-university-
main-campus-in-marawi-city-has-been-awarded-as-the/4837256936329044/</ref>
His administration also advanced the system's pursuit of Level IV accreditation (the highest AACCUP tier,
benchmarked against excellent foreign universities), with key programs at MSU-Iligan Institute of Technology
(MSU-IIT) reaching or maintaining that elite status during his tenure.
These programs included Bachelor of Arts in English, Filipino, History, Political Science, and Sociology; Bachelor
of Science in Psychology; Bachelor of Secondary Education; and Bachelor of Teacher Technology Education.

PAGE 5
At the same time, his administration pursued Certificate of Program Compliance (COPC) from the Commission
on Higher Education (CHED) across the system, with MSU-Tawi-Tawi achieving a landmark 100% COPC
compliance for all undergraduate programs evaluated, and MSU-Marawi advancing compliance in programs such
as BS Environmental Science, BS Fisheries, BS Psychology, BS Mathematics, and BS Statistics.<ref
name="msutcto">MSU-TCTO. (n.d.). MSU-TCTO achieves 100% Certificate of Program Compliance.
https://msutcto.edu.ph/msu-tcto-achieves-100-certificate-of-program-compliance-on-all-undergraduate-programs-
evaluated</ref><ref name="msumain-accred">Mindanao State University Main Campus. (n.d.). MSU's
accreditation pursuit: two days of intensive program evaluation and review. https://www.msumain.edu.ph/msus-
accreditation-pursuit-two-days-of-intensive-program-evaluation-and-review/</ref>
Summary of Accreditation Milestones During the Macaayong Presidency (2016–2022)
Category
Highlights
Level IV
(AACCUP)
BA English, BA Political Science, BA History, BS Psychology, Secondary Education (primarily at
MSU-IIT)
COPC (CHED)
BS Agriculture, BS Forestry, BS Environmental Science, BS Business Administration; 100%
compliance at MSU-TCTO
Growth Milestone
40 programs reached Level I status by 2021, ranking MSU-Marawi No. 1 among SUCs nationally
Values and Leadership Philosophy
Dr. Macaayong's approach to leadership was shaped by two values he held consistently throughout his career:
meritocracy and compassion.
He believed in rewarding hard work and qualifications with promotions and opportunities, as the faculty promotion
drive demonstrated. But he also believed that compassion, especially toward students navigating poverty and crisis,
had to be built into institutional policy, not just personal kindness.
That combination, principled structure paired with human warmth, is what many colleagues and students point to
when they describe his leadership style.
His time as a peace negotiator deepened this. He'd spent years at the table between the government and the MILF,
working on questions about who gets power and how it's shared. He understood that institutions either build trust or
erode it, and he was determined that MSU would keep building it.
Legacy
Dr. Habib Watamama Macaayong leaves behind a university system that is more accredited, better staffed, and
more physically equipped than the one he inherited.
He steered MSU through the Marawi Siege and the COVID-19 pandemic, two of the most disruptive events in the
university's modern history, and in both cases came out with the institution's mission intact and even strengthened.
His "Balik MSU" campaign is remembered not just as an operational success but as a cultural moment: a Meranaw
institution declaring, in the aftermath of war, that education would not be surrendered to extremism.
The more than 900 faculty members who received long-overdue promotions during his watch, the 40 programs that
achieved AACCUP Level I status, the fiber optic cables running across the Marawi campus, and the students who
graduated during the pandemic under the Mass Promotion policy are all part of the same legacy: a university that

PAGE 6
refused to stand still.
He is the Peace President of Mindanao State University, a title earned not in ceremony but in action, across thirty-
five years of teaching, a decade of peace negotiations, and six years at the helm of one of the Philippines' most
storied state universities.
Recognition
Named the Top 1 Performing SUC in the Philippines under the AACCUP accreditation system by 2021,
under his leadership as MSU System President.<ref name="fb-msumain"/>
Recognized nationally for his role as chairman of the technical working group on power sharing during the
GPH-MILF peace negotiations (2004 to 2013).
Credited by colleagues and the MSU community as the driving force behind the most comprehensive faculty
promotion initiative in the university's recent history.
Challenges
No honest account of Dr. Macaayong's presidency skips over the controversy surrounding his appointment.
His naming as MSU System President drew public criticism in some quarters, with questions raised about the
selection process and the politics surrounding university leadership appointments.<ref name="inquirer-naming"/>
Beyond the appointment, governing a university in an active conflict zone presented challenges that no policy
manual fully prepares a president for. The Marawi Siege tested every institutional system the university had, from
its security protocols to its student records to its administrative continuity.
The COVID-19 pandemic added a second layer of disruption just as the university was rebuilding, forcing difficult
decisions about academic standards, student welfare, and institutional survival.
That he navigated both without the university losing its footing says something about the depth of institutional trust
he had built and the resilience of the community around him.

text:
PAGE 1

Occupation

Peace Advocate
Known For

Manila Bulletin Mindanao
bureau; chronicler of the
Bangsamoro peace process
Region

Manila Times; Philippine

Recognition
