University, Cairo (B.S. Islamic Studies;
M.A. Islamic Philosophy)
Award
Golden Amazing Leaders in Islam (ALI)
Awardee, 2016 — Golden Crescent
Consortium of Peace Builders and Affiliates
Inc.
Notability
Zamboangueño Banguingui Islamic scholar
and jurist; First Grand Mufti of Southern
Philippines; Al-Azhar-trained theologian;
EDUCATION
His religious formation began at a remarkably young age. At
nine years old, his uncle Sheikh Jamil brought him as a pilgrim
to the Holy Land, where he was placed in the care of an Arab
family and enrolled in the prestigious Al-Falah Islamic School in
Mecca. This was no ordinary enrollment: the school was, at the
time, open exclusively to Arab students, making young
Abdulgani the sole non-Arab student in the institution. His
immersion in the Arabic language and Islamic tradition was so
complete that he would later quip with characteristic wit: "My
father is an Arab from the Philippines." He spent his formative
years in Mecca during an era before the oil era had transformed
the city. The holy shrines were lit by kerosene lamps, and the
atmosphere was one of deep austerity and devotion, a fitting
crucible for the scholar he was becoming.
At nineteen, he journeyed to Cairo and enrolled at Al-Azhar
University, then already more than a thousand years old and the
foremost center of Sunni Islamic learning in the world. He
completed a degree in Islamic Studies and a Master's degree in
Islamic Philosophy, with specializations in Fiqh (Islamic
Jurisprudence) and Usulud-Din (the Roots of Religion, covering
Islamic Theology and Creed). His academic distinction was
remarkable: at his graduation in 1964, he was singled out as the
only Asian student to receive the President Gamal Abdel Nasser
Award in Theology, placing him among the finest scholars
produced by Al-Azhar in his generation.
Before returning home, he traveled extensively to Islamic
educational centers across the world, studying how each
institution functioned and gathering insights that would later
shape his vision for Islamic education in the Philippines.
CAREER
Upon completing his studies, Abdulgani Yusop was offered the
opportunity to serve as a missionary to any Arabic-speaking
country in Africa, a position of considerable honor from Al-
Azhar. He declined. His heart was set on Mindanao, and he
returned home with a firm conviction that the Muslim people of
the Philippines were on the threshold of an Islamic revival.
His first major contribution upon return was in education.
Drawing on his observations of Islamic institutions around the
world, he established several Islamic madrasahs across the
region. Chief among them was the Zambasul Ulama Center for
Arabic and Islamic Studies, which became a foundational
institution for Islamic learning in Western Mindanao.

PAGE 3
Founder, Darul Ifta' Region IX and
Palawan; Interfaith peacebuilder during
the Mindanao armed conflict
Known For
Founding the Darul Ifta' Region IX and
Palawan (1989); landmark 1974 interfaith
gesture with Archbishop Cruces during Eid
al-Fitr; President Gamal Abdel Nasser
Award in Theology at Al-Azhar (1964);
establishing the Zambasul Ulama Center
for Arabic and Islamic Studies
In 1989, he was unanimously elected by a Mindanao-wide
conference of Ulama as Grand Mufti for Southern Philippines,
the highest religious office for Muslims in the region. As
founder and first Grand Mufti of the Darul Ifta' Region IX and
Palawan, he institutionalized a framework of religious authority
grounded in the Ahlussunnah wal Jama'ah tradition: Ash'ari in
creed, Shafi'i in jurisprudence, and balanced in its embrace of
the spiritual sciences of Tasawwuf.
Throughout his tenure and beyond, he served as a trusted arbiter
in religious disputes, a counselor to government leaders, and a
guide to the Mujahideen. He was known for welcoming all who
came to his door, receiving them with a cup of tea and the
unhurried wisdom of a man fully at peace with his knowledge.
Those who knew him said simply: he was a man for all seasons.
INSTITUTIONAL CONTRIBUTIONS
Darul Ifta' Region IX and Palawan
The Darul Ifta' Region IX and Palawan, which Grand Mufti Abdulgani Yusop founded in 1989, remains the most
significant institutional legacy of his leadership. As the Supreme Council for Islamic Preaching and Guidance for
the Zamboanga Peninsula and Palawan, it has served as the religious backbone of Muslim communities in the
region for more than three decades after his tenure. The creed, jurisprudence, and spiritual orientation he embedded
in the institution, Ash'ari, Shafi'i, and Sufi, remain its defining character to this day.
Zambasul Ulama Center for Arabic and Islamic Studies
Among the madrasahs he established, the Zambasul Ulama Center for Arabic and Islamic Studies stands out as a
cornerstone of Islamic learning in Western Mindanao. The Center trained generations of scholars and teachers, and
its graduates have gone on to serve Muslim communities across the region.
Mentorship and Scholarly Formation
His students include Senior Sunni Sufi Scholar Sayyiduna Shaykh Khadraji Guru Bata Tapsi Al Ash'ari Ash Shafi'i
(Ameer of Sabielal Muhatadin) and former NCMF Commissioner and Sunni Sufi Scholar Prof. Yusuf Morales,
figures who themselves became pillars of Islamic scholarship in the region.
PEACE ADVOCACY AND INTERFAITH DIALOGUE
Grand Mufti Abdulgani Yusop is perhaps best remembered for his extraordinary acts of peacemaking during one of
the darkest chapters of Mindanao's history. In 1974, at the height of the armed conflict in Mindanao, he invited
Archbishop Cruces to join him inside the masjid during the Eid al-Fitr prayers, following the month of Ramadan
fasting, at Campo Muslim, Zamboanga City. In that single gesture, a Muslim Grand Mufti welcoming a Catholic
Archbishop into the house of Islamic worship at its holiest moment, he sent an unmistakable message to both
communities: the war was not between Muslims and Christians, and it was not a religious war. It was driven by
political causes, and the path forward lay in mutual understanding, not mutual fear.

PAGE 4
He was a central figure in many peace mediation panels, a constant partner in efforts to bring lasting peace to
Mindanao. He taught that the resolution of conflict required a genuine recognition of the culture of unity in
diversity, and that peaceful coexistence was not merely a political arrangement but a spiritual obligation rooted in
Islamic teaching.
SCHOLARLY TEACHINGS
His teachings on prayer, Quranic recitation, trust in God, and the ethics of conduct have been preserved and passed
down through his students and community.
Among his most celebrated instructions was his guidance on approaching the Quran with progressive depths of
consciousness:
"Make it a habit to read daily the Holy Quran, and consciously when you read — as if you were
hearing the Holy Prophet narrate those verses to his followers; then as if you were hearing the
Archangel Gabriel narrate those verses to the Holy Prophet; then as if you were hearing Allah narrate
those verses to Archangel Gabriel; then as if you were hearing Allah narrate those verses directly to
you; then finally, as if you were hearing the voice and the verses are One... It will penetrate into your
core and you internalize its teachings and grasp some of its hidden treasures."
On the purpose of prayer, he taught:
"The end result of Salah is enjoining good and forbidding evil. When we still do evil, not doing good
deeds to ourselves, to our families, to our fellow humans and other creation — then know that our
Salah have not been accepted yet."
On the ethics of integrity and trust in God:
"Be the tricked (betrayed/fooled) rather than the treacherous. Leave all your affairs to Allah, and do
not seek revenge."
On the nature of knowledge:
"There are many knowledgeable now, yet only a few are keen in understanding."
LEGACY
The legacy of Grand Mufti Abdulgani L. Yusop Al-Haj is not preserved in monuments but in people: in the scholars
he trained, the communities he guided, the institution he founded, and the vision of Islamic leadership he
embodied. He demonstrated that a Muslim scholar can be simultaneously a man of the highest learning and the
deepest humility, a guardian of classical tradition and an active agent of modern peacebuilding.
He is remembered not merely for what he achieved but for how he lived: welcoming everyone at his doorstep,
joking gently with the young, never turning away the elders who sought to learn, receiving the mighty and the
struggling with equal grace. He was, in the words of those who loved him, a man for all seasons, his character
seasoned by a knowledge of Islam that was not merely intellectual but transformative.
His life demonstrated in practice what he preached in teaching: that scholarship serves humanity, that peace is a
religious duty, and that the greatest leaders are those who make themselves servants of all.
May Allah be pleased with his soul, and may his legacy continue to illuminate the path of those who follow.

PAGE 5

Lumna G. Zaman
Dr. Lumna G. Zaman (born February 6, 1946) is a Filipino
Muslim educator, academic administrator, and international
education consultant whose career has centered on the advancement
of education and higher learning in the Philippines and Southeast
Asia.
He was born in Ditsa'an-Ramain, Lanao del Sur, and belongs to the
Maranao ethnic group. He is married to Hadjah Rohaneza "Rocaya"

EARLY LIFE AND EDUCATION
Dr. Zaman completed his elementary education at Marawi Central
Elementary Pilot School in Marawi City from 1954 to 1960. He
then attended Dansalan Junior College in Marawi City for his first
three years of secondary school, from 1960 to 1963, before
completing his fourth year at Jamiatul Philippine Al-Islamia, where
he graduated in 1964.
He pursued his college education at Notre Dame University in
Cotabato City, earning a Bachelor of Arts degree in 1969 with a
major in Political Science and a minor in English. He went on to St.
Michael's College in Iligan City, where he completed a Master of
Arts in Education in 1977, majoring in Administration and
Supervision with a minor in Guidance and Counselling. He later
earned his Doctor of Philosophy in Education at Xavier University
in Cagayan de Oro City in 1989, majoring in Management.

CAREER
Jamiatul Philippine Al-Islamia
Dr. Zaman began his career as a high school classroom teacher at
Jamiatul Philippine Al-Islamia in 1969, the same institution where
he had completed his secondary education a few years earlier. From
1969 to 1974, he also served as Commandant of the school's PMTC
program and as Senior Tactical Officer for its ROTC unit from 1970
to 1974.
He moved into academic leadership in 1973, becoming Assistant
Principal of the High School Department, then College Instructor in
1974. That same year, he was named Assistant Dean of Colleges, a
post he held until 1977. He served as Director for the Summer
Institute in 1976 and again in 1983, and took on the role of Officer-
in-Charge (OIC President) of the institution from 1977 to 1978,
followed by a term as Acting Vice President for Academic Affairs
from 1978 to 1979.
From 1976 to 1981, Dr. Zaman served as Dean of Colleges. He then transitioned into the Graduate School as
Professor from 1984 to 1991, and took on consultancy roles within the institution, serving as Administrative
Consultant from 1990 to 1994 and as Consultant for the Higher Education Department from 1995 to 1996. He
capped his service at Jamiatul Philippine Al-Islamia as Vice President for Academic Affairs from 1997 to 1999.
Across more than two decades at the institution, Dr. Zaman held nearly every major academic leadership post
available, reflecting a long and steady rise through the ranks of one of Marawi City's pioneering educational
institutions.
Mindanao State University
Dr. Zaman's affiliation with Mindanao State University began in 1981, when he joined as Assistant Professor in the
undergraduate and graduate programs. He was promoted to Associate Professor in 1982 and, in the same year, took
on the additional role of Special Assistant in the Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, a post he held
until 1984.
He became Chairman of the Graduate Education Department from 1990 to 1993, and briefly served as Officer-in-
Charge of the Office of the Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs (OIC-OVCAA) in 1998. He was named full
Professor at the Graduate School in 1994, a position he held until 1999.
Dr. Zaman's tenure at MSU reached its peak when he was appointed Assistant Dean of the Graduate School in
1997, and then Dean of the Graduate School in 1999, serving in that capacity until 2001.
International consultancy in Indonesia
The claim below regarding Dr. Zaman's role as Team Leader of the ADB-financed Madrasah Aliyah
Development Project (Loan No. 1519-INO) could not be independently verified through available public
ADB or academic records, and is presented here strictly as submitted by the source material pending
confirmation.

According to source material submitted for this profile, during his tenure as Dean of the Graduate School, Dr.
Zaman was granted a sabbatical leave to serve as Team Leader of the International Consultants for the
Development of the Madrasah Aliyah Project in Indonesia, a project said to be financed by the Asian Development
Bank (ADB) under Loan No. 1519-INO and implemented by Indonesia's Ministry of Religious Affairs from 1999
to 2001. The project is described as one of Indonesia's most significant educational reform initiatives for Islamic
secondary education at the time.
As Team Leader, Dr. Zaman is said to have headed an international team of consultants from various countries, a
distinction that would have made him one of the few Filipinos entrusted with leading a major international
education project of this scale. Under his leadership, the consultancy team is described as having assisted in
modernizing Indonesia's Madrasah Aliyah system, with work spanning the improvement of academic standards in
science, mathematics, English, and other general education subjects while preserving Islamic values, the
establishment of 35 Model Madrasah Aliyah Negeri (MAN) as centers of excellence, the training of professors,
teachers, and school administrators, the improvement of educational management systems, and the development of
policies, implementation manuals, and technical recommendations submitted to both Indonesia's Ministry of
Religious Affairs and the Asian Development Bank.
If confirmed, this appointment would represent a distinction not only for Mindanao State University but for the
Philippines more broadly, illustrating the capacity of Filipino Muslim educators to lead international educational
reform efforts.
TEACHING LEGACY
Over more than thirty years as an educator, Dr. Zaman taught at the secondary, undergraduate, master's, and
doctoral levels. His students went on to become educators, professionals, religious scholars, government officials,
and community leaders across Lanao del Sur and beyond.
For several decades, Dr. Zaman was regarded as one of the most esteemed educators in the Province of Lanao del
Sur. Many professionals and leaders from the province who pursued their education during the 1970s through the
1990s passed through his classrooms at some point in their academic journey, contributing in no small way to the
intellectual and educational development of the Bangsamoro people.
PERSONAL LIFE
Dr. Zaman is married to Hadjah Rohaneza "Rocaya" Ibrahim Zaman. He practices Islam and identifies as Maranao.
LEGACY
Through his decades of service as a professor, university administrator, institutional leader, and (per submitted
source material, pending verification) international consultant, Dr. Lumna G. Zaman is remembered as a
foundational figure in the development of education in Marawi City and Lanao del Sur. His career reflects the
broader story of Maranao educators who built and sustained institutions of higher learning in the Bangsamoro
region across the second half of the twentieth century.
